resources.name: Crystal structure of O-Ti₂AlNb (Cmcm, from Mozer et al. 1990)

access.notes: Orthorhombic structure, space group Cmcm (No. 63), 4 formula units per cell. Atomic positions from the literature (e.g., Mozer et al., Scr. Metall. Mater. 24 (1990) 2363) or from ICSD. The structure description must be obtainable from publicly available crystallographic databases.

resources.notes: Used as the starting structure for the O‑Ti₂AlNb geometry optimization.

resources.name: AlCu₂Mn Heusler prototype structure (Fm‑3m)

access.notes: Standard Heusler structure with Wyckoff positions 4a (0,0,0) for Al, 4b (½,½,½) for Nb, and 8c (¼,¼,¼) for Ti. Available from standard crystal structure databases or the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database (ICSD).

resources.notes: Used to construct the H1 and H2 modifications of Ti₂AlNb.

resources.name: Open‑source DFT code (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO, CP2K, ABINIT)

access.notes: Any open‑source periodic DFT package capable of geometry optimization with hybrid functionals (B3LYP) is acceptable. The paper used the proprietary CRYSTAL17 code; the agent must re‑implement with this publicly available tool.

resources.name: Standard pseudopotentials/basis sets for Ti, Al, Nb

access.notes: Use standard pseudopotential libraries (e.g., PBE PAW, B3LYP PAW) appropriate for the chosen DFT code. The paper used all‑electron basis sets; open‑source equivalents such as PAW pseudopotentials from standard repositories (e.g., GBRV, SSSP) are acceptable.
